senses.sense_definition: Relating to or providing a brief summary or general overview of something.

examples.text: The report provides a <w>synoptic</w> view of the company's performance over the last decade.
She gave a <w>synoptic</w> account of the events that led to the sudden resignation.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to data collected simultaneously over a large area to provide a broad picture of atmospheric conditions.

examples.text: Meteorologists use <w>synoptic</w> charts to track the movement of large weather systems.
The <w>synoptic</w> observation showed a significant drop in pressure across the entire region.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the first three books of the New Testament, which share a similar perspective and narrative structure.

examples.text: Scholars often compare the <w>synoptic</w> gospels to identify common sources used by the authors.
The <w>synoptic</w> tradition emphasizes the teachings and ministry of Jesus in Galilee.

senses.sense_definition: One of the first three books of the New Testament.

examples.text: The professor explained how each of the <w>Synoptics</w> presents a unique theological focus.
Many students find it difficult to reconcile the differences between the <w>Synoptics</w> and the Gospel of John.
